articles.title: RBI raises share of domestically held gold reserves, data shows
articles.excerpt:
As of September, the Reserve Bank of India has expanded its domestic gold reserves to 880.52 metric tonnes. This figure comprises 740.13 metric tonnes held in the country and 140.39 metric tonnes stored internationally. However, the proportion of gold within the overall reserves has declined to 14.38%. Currently, India's total foreign exchange reserves stand at $705.3 billion, predominantly invested in foreign government securities.
